items.title: Carney government weakening pesticide regulation, warns Green Party Leader Elizabeth May
items.author: Eric Klempan
items.excerpt: Buried in Bill C-31, a budget implementation bill tabled in May and currently under consideration, is a weakening of Canada’s pesticide evaluation standards.
items.leadExcerpt: The initiative follows Bill C-30, which passed last June. Among new budgetary measures, C-30 amended the Pest Control Products Act (PCPA), allowing the federal government to temporarily authorize the use of any pesticide, including those that have been deemed unsafe by Health Canada.

items.title: Quebec expects direct consultation on Erasmus+
items.author: Aidan Raynor
items.excerpt: The extent of Canada’s participation in Erasmus+ has yet to be determined, but no matter where those negotiations lead, Quebec’s Ministry of Higher Education expects to be “consulted directly.”
items.leadExcerpt: “Our government is open to learning from other post-secondary systems and exploring opportunities that make sense and provide value for Albertans. It is too early to say what Canada’s potential participation in Erasmus+ could mean for Alberta,” said McDougall in a statement to The Concordian.

items.title: As Big Tech invests more in eye-tracking tools, Canadians’ data is left unprotected
items.author: Chloe Rose Stuart-Ulin
items.excerpt: According to experts, eye movement data can reveal a lot about us, from our age range to our sexual preferences. Some research suggests it could serve as a unique biometric identifier.
items.leadExcerpt: Research shows the potential for patterns of eye movement to distinguish children from adults, reveal someone’s gender, sexual preferences and signs of neurodivergence. Other research suggests a person’s eye movements might also serve as a unique biometric identifier, much like a fingerprint.

items.title: Two federal byelections to take place in Montreal on Dec. 7
items.author: Samuel Vandenberg
items.excerpt: A total of six byelections will be held across the country in December, filling seats left vacant by departed MPs from the Liberals, Conservatives, NDP and the Bloc Québécois.
items.leadExcerpt: The ridings holding elections in Montreal will be Rosemont—La Petite-Patrie and Laurier–Sainte-Marie. Both seats were left vacant following the departure of their former members of parliament (MPs) this past summer.

items.title: If Quebec stops the clocks, should they be frozen on standard or daylight savings time?
items.author: Robin Hill
items.excerpt: Though Quebec is commonly affiliated with a desire to operate independently from the rest of Canada, the long-standing debate regarding time change has led to an instance of Quebec seeming to follow in other provinces’ footsteps.

items.title: Albania’s “Flamingo Revolution” enters its ninth month
items.author: Léo Vallet David
items.excerpt: Thousands of Albanians marched through the streets of Albania’s capital, Tirana, on Nov. 2, demanding the removal of the country’s prime minister, Edi Rama. The movement has now entered its ninth month.

items.title: What does rejecting AI actually look like?
items.author: Saima Mazumder
items.excerpt: As the use of artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly common at Concordia, some students are raising concerns about its role in their academics. They have begun turning their opposition into collective action through the “It’s time to change AI discourse” initiative.

items.title: Renovated facilities and new funding strategies planned for the CRA in upcoming academic year
items.author: Anthony Maruca
items.excerpt: Concordia University’s Recreation and Athletics department (CRA) plans to invest its resources in repurposing existing facilities and identifying new revenue streams while keeping as much traditionally outsourced work internally.

items.title: Commemorating 50 years of Concordia’s men’s soccer national championship title
items.author: Anthony Tapia Ancinez
items.excerpt: On Nov. 14, 1976, two years after the merger of Sir George Williams University and Loyola College, the Concordia Stingers men’s soccer team won the Canadian Interuniversity Athletic Union (CIAU) National Championship, now known as the U Sports National Championship, for the

items.title: Cavalry runs over FC Supra du Québec in playoff semifinal
items.author: Anthony Tapia Ancinez
items.excerpt: FC Supra du Québec made history after qualifying for the Canadian Premier League (CPL) playoffs in their debut season. Despite losing to Cavalry FC 3–2 on aggregate, the team has shown that a fully Québécois roster can compete at the national level.

items.title: CF Montréal is up for sale
items.author: The editorial team
items.excerpt: Club owner Joey Saputo did not rule out selling to buyers who would move the team, though it would not be his preference.

items.title: Les étudiants québécois solidaires avec la jeunesse française
items.author: Léo Vallet David
items.excerpt: En France, la génération Z se mobilise depuis quelques mois. Partout dans le pays, des étudiants bloquent les campus et manifestent leur mécontentement à l’égard du gouvernement d’Emmanuel Macron.

items.title: « C’est la faute des écrans! »
items.author: Maud Peiffer
items.excerpt: Ce n’est un secret pour personne : la démocratie est malade. Et comme le disait Camus : « Quand une démocratie est malade, le fascisme vient à son chevet, mais ce n’est pas pour prendre de ses nouvelles. »

items.title: Jusqu’où peut-on innover tout en respectant la vie privée?
items.author: Marie-Laurence Roy-Miquelon
items.excerpt: Invitée à l’Université Concordia le 29 octobre dernier dans le cadre du programme juriste en résidence, l’avocate Éloïse Gratton, figure majeure du droit de la vie privée au Canada, a abordé les défis de son domaine. Selon elle, la vie privée se situe aujourd’hui à

items.title: Why is everybody a DJ?
items.author: Aidan Flanagan
items.excerpt: A new Montreal DJ comes out of the woodwork daily. Industry professionals say accessibility, tangibility and storytelling make DJing so popular.

items.title: KATSEYE brings their WILDWORLD TOUR to Montreal
items.author: Veronica Rebuli
items.excerpt: On the road for their WILDWORLD TOUR, KATSEYE stopped in Montreal on Oct. 30 to deliver dance-filled performances with a spooky twist. The global girl group brought their latest EP, WILD, to the stage, treating fans to an evening of energetic pop music and polished choreography.

items.title: QUICKSPINS: Bktherula — N5ON
items.author: Aidan Flanagan
items.excerpt: Bktherula has always been a pioneer, making space for women artists in rap’s growing “rage” subgenre. On her fifth studio album, N5ON, she attempts to take that pioneering spirit a step further with some genre-bending.

items.title: Reel Picks: “For the love of noir!”
items.author: Veronica Rebuli
items.excerpt: Emerging from postwar Hollywood and reimagined through neo-noir, the genre continues to expose the darker side of human nature.

items.title: Human Connection: No plus one required
items.author: Brandy Mitchell
items.excerpt: Since launching in 2025, Montreal’s Human Connection, a social experience company, has hosted events across the city to make it easier for adults to make new friends by encouraging attendees to come alone, socialize and leave with new connections.

items.title: The magic of world-building through art
items.author: Julia Imee Silva
items.excerpt: Kira-Madina Storch builds worlds of mythology and fiction using paint and canvas. Her imagination wanders down a magical rabbit hole, represented in images that hang on the gallery wall.

items.title: If you don’t know the answer, AI does
items.author: Rita Kamel
items.excerpt: Last week, I went to pull up my last article online just like I usually do; I searched my name and added The Concordian so my article could pop up, but it didn’t. Instead, I saw an AI overview with my name on it and information about me — that was the creepiest thing ever.

items.title: No one wants to grow old anymore
items.author: Anabel Blanchette-Glaude
items.excerpt: Tell a child your age, and they will tell you that you are old. This is not a fact, but a universal experience.

items.title: Why Remembrance Day still matters, now more than ever
items.author: Dominic Corbett
items.excerpt: The deaths of four Canadian soldiers at CFB Wainwright are a stark reminder that military service is not merely history. As Canadians prepare to mark Remembrance Day, remembering those who serve and those who never come home is more important than ever.

items.title: A year with Soraya Martinez Ferrada
items.author: Julia Miller
items.excerpt: What Montrealers think about the change of power in the city Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada before a meeting with former Quebec Premier Christine Fréchette at Montreal City Hall on Sept. 18, 2026. Photo Nicolas Tremblay This article originally appeared in The Link Volume
items.leadExcerpt: Mayor Martinez Ferrada has implemented policies since she was elected to address poverty, focusing on financial incentives. Her administration has increased the budget for the unhoused crisis and has allowed people living in encampments at specific sites to stay rather than being removed.

items.title: Concordia’s deficit detrimental to student experience
items.author: Callista Mille
items.excerpt: Complaints about Concordia’s building maintenance and reduced campus services continue to persist On Oct. 15, yellow caution cones surrounded a leaking water fountain on the seventh floor of the Henry F. Hall Building. Photo Callista Mille This article originally appeared in The
items.leadExcerpt: Students at Concordia University are still affected by the university’s ongoing deficit, which was intensified by government changes and tuition hikes. Concordia’s recovery plan to eliminate this deficit by 2028-2029 is actively straining the quality of its operational services.

items.title: What does it mean for students if Canada joins the Erasmus+ exchange program?
items.author: Santiago Sánchez Arbouin
items.excerpt: Going on exchange to Europe could be the bridge to deepen transatlantic relations With increasing ties between Europe and Canada, Canadian students might be able to join the Erasmus exchange program. Graphic Aia Segal This article originally appeared in The Link Volume 47, Issue
items.leadExcerpt: In the United States-Canada trade war, it is tricky to define a “winning” side. However, Canada is developing a unique relationship with Europe, one that could help Canada gain inclusion in the Erasmus+ exchange program. Canadian universities currently manage their exchange programs directly through bilateral agreements between institutions. This limits not only student mobility but also the funding available for them.

items.title: Advocates urge new Quebec government to end cooperation with Israel
items.author: Rahul Balasundaram
items.excerpt: The Votons Palestine campaign outlined four key demands ahead of the provincial election Advocates are demanding the Parti Québécois government take measures to avoid complicity in genocide and apartheid and give equal healthcare coverage to residents from Gaza. Photo Nicolas
items.leadExcerpt: The demands of the campaign include closing Quebec’s office in Tel Aviv, divesting from companies complicit in violating international law through the Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec (CDPQ), ending the flow of military equipment to Israel and extending healthcare coverage to residents arriving in Quebec from Gaza.

items.title: Editorial: Sweeping away the dead Republican leaves
items.author: The editorial team
items.excerpt: Two protesters surrounded by tourists in front of the White House on June 7, 2026 in Washington D.C. Photo Nicolas Tremblay This article originally appeared in The Link Volume 47, Issue 5, published November 10, 2026.
items.leadExcerpt: United States President Donald Trump’s second term has been a political disaster for the U.S. He’s left the country’s people, and the world as a whole, feeling politically hopeless.

items.title: Montreal Roses advance to the 2026 NSL final
items.author: Nicolas Tremblay
items.excerpt: Montreal showed its thorns in the semi-final, winning 5-2 across both legs against the Vancouver Rise Montreal Roses and Vancouver Rise FC both played a physically and technically tied matchup on Nov. 8, 2026 at Stade Boréale. Photo Yann Rifflard
items.leadExcerpt: The Montreal Roses have reached the Northern Super League (NSL) final in their second season. Montreal won its semi-final matchups by an aggregate score of 5-2 against Vancouver Rise FC, moving on after a 2-2 tie on Nov. 8 at Stade Boréale.
